A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DenseDPO work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation benchmarks, human evaluations, preference-prediction experiments, ablations, and the Flux-based empirical analysis in Appendix B.2.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, guidance-data robustness results, GPT-label scaling experiments, and reported failed approaches.

M1.justification: Guided pair generation, segment-level preference optimization, the underlying video model, and GPT labeling remain unchanged. Equations (5)–(7), Algorithms 1–2, and Appendix E pseudocode retain the same procedures; the additional methods are experimental comparators.

E1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly documents preliminary experimentation on VBench's own prompt suite, with a qualitative observation about high scores despite degraded motion. The principal VideoJAM-bench and MotionBench coverage, training corpus, and Flux analysis remain unchanged. Additional subsampling experiments do not introduce new domains.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds evaluated D3PO, DPOK, and SePPO comparators, extending the original comparison to online reinforcement learning and semi-policy preference optimization. Table 4 also adds the pretrained reference to the ablation comparison. The original benchmark and VLM comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments vary GPT-label quantities across 10k, 35k, and 55k and substitute a disjoint 10k guidance-video subset. Added baseline protocols include DPOK with VisionReward feedback and a 2 × 10^-6 learning rate. Existing benchmark prompts, metrics, DenseDPO training settings, and inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds tests of dependence on guidance-video selection and automatic-label quantity, addressing robustness and scalability of central components. Appendices A.2 and C.4 add qualitative failures of REFL and real-video-winning preference pairs. The segment-length ablation is relocated from v1 Appendix C.3; unequal-guidance failure was already described in v1 Appendix A.2.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five generation seeds per prompt in Appendix A.5. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical aggregation across training runs are introduced. The disjoint guidance-data experiment is a robustness control rather than a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds the New GT Video results, GPT-label scaling results, and scores for three additional baselines. For example, Table 6 reports visual quality of 0.247 for 10k GPT labels, alongside the retained 55k result of 0.368; Table 7 reports DPOK dynamic degree of 0.457 under VisionReward. These are additional experimental conditions, not improvements to the unchanged headline results in Tables 1–3.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, definitions, and Appendix B derivation and assumptions are retained. Section 3.1 clarifies the forward-process and denoising explanation without changing the formal mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: motion-preserving guided pairs, denser temporal supervision, improved data efficiency, and automatic VLM annotation. The revised conclusion repeats the VLM contribution already claimed in v1 rather than introducing a new core claim.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new controls as evidence of guidance-data robustness and compensation for noisy GPT labels through scale. It adds explanations for DPOK, SePPO, REFL, and real-video-winning failures. Appendix D replaces the prompt-perturbation extension with a proposal for dense VLM rewards in online RL; existing principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds implementation-source links for D3PO and DPOK, D3PO's reuse of VanillaDPO labels, DPOK's reward model and learning rate, and SePPO's reimplementation status. The DPOK KL weight is described without a numerical value. Existing DenseDPO hyperparameters, hardware information, prompt templates, and pseudocode are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to PatchDPO, SePPO, Step-Video-T2V, Flow-GRPO, and DanceGRPO, and expands discussion of online alignment alternatives. The central positioning around motion bias and temporal preference granularity is unchanged. Publication metadata updates and removal of a duplicate Emu entry do not constitute substantive changes.

P1.justification: v2 revises the method introduction and background explanation, expands Section 4.4, adds appendix subsections for additional baselines and failed attempts, and moves the segment-length discussion into the main text. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6 and 7, expands Table 4, and moves v1 Table 6 into the main text as Table 5. The existing figures and their scientific content are retained, with changes to placement, table formatting, captions, and document layout.

improvement.justification: The additional baselines, guidance-data control, and GPT-label scaling experiment strengthen empirical support and clarify the data requirements of automatic annotation. Reporting failed approaches also improves transparency. These are useful, targeted gains over an already substantial evaluation; the main results and theory remain unchanged, while documentation of the added baseline settings remains incomplete.
